name: Follow-Up
lineup: Every unsold estimate gets a follow-up cadence. Drafts are written overnight in your voice and go out when you approve them.

seo.title: Follow-Up — Kickback
seo.description: Follow-Up enrolls every unsold estimate from your CRM, drafts each day's texts and emails overnight, and queues them for your reps to send from their own Gmail and phone.
seo.ogDescription: Every unsold estimate gets a cadence. Drafts are ready each morning, and nothing goes to a customer until a rep sends it.

hero.lede: Follow-Up enrolls each unsold estimate from your CRM, writes the day's texts and emails overnight, and lines them up in one Outbox. Your reps read each one and send it from their own Gmail and phone.

sections.title: Works With
sections.note: Emails go out through each rep's own Gmail. Siro call recordings tell the drafts what the customer said on the visit.

sections.title: Your Follow-Up List, Written Every Morning
sections.lede: Connect your CRM, Gmail and Siro once. After that, the only screen your reps need is the Outbox.

items.title: Estimates Enroll
items.body: After each CRM sync, every unsold estimate joins Follow-Up. A rep confirms it with one tap and the cadence starts. Won, lost and canceled estimates stay out.

items.title: Drafts Are Written Overnight
items.body: At 4am your time, Kickback writes a text and an email for every touch due that day, using the quote, the call recording and a photo or video from your library.

items.title: Reps Send and Log
items.body: Reps call, send and log each touch from the Outbox. Turn on activity notes and every logged touch is added to the estimate in your CRM.

items.title: Estimates Enroll Themselves
items.body: You choose when an estimate enrolls: when it's created, when the visit is scheduled, or after the visit. From there its cadence decides when to reach out and whether to call, text or email. Owners can change the days and channels of each cadence.

bullets.title: The Standard Sequence
bullets.text: Four touches over 14 days. Day 1 is a call and a text, day 3 a call and an email, and days 7 and 14 use all three.

bullets.title: Statuses Pick the Next Touch
bullets.text: Log Thinking after a call and the estimate moves to lighter check-ins on day 6 and day 10. A date from the customer moves it to Date Given, with the next touch on that day.

bullets.title: Nurture Catches the Rest
bullets.text: When a sequence ends without a decision, the estimate moves to Nurture, with touches on day 30, 60 and 90.

bullets.title: Won and Lost Come From Your CRM
bullets.text: Approve an option or mark the estimate lost in your CRM, and Follow-Up closes it on the next sync.

items.title: Drafts Written Overnight in Your Voice
items.body: Each draft is written in first person from the rep who owns the estimate and mentions a real detail from the quote. Texts stay under 320 characters, emails run 60 to 150 words, and the drafter is told never to make up a price, discount or deadline.

bullets.title: What Was Said on the Visit
bullets.text: Connect Siro and the summary of the sales call goes into the draft, along with details like budget and timeline. The recording itself is never quoted.

bullets.title: Your Own Photos and Videos
bullets.text: Upload job photos and videos to the Media Library. Kickback tags each upload and attaches the best match to the text and email, with a one-line reason for the pick.

bullets.title: Rewrite on Request
bullets.text: Edit any draft or press Regenerate. In the iPhone app, ask for it shorter, more casual, with the price, or pushing for a decision.

items.title: The Outbox
items.body: Each rep works one queue of today's touches, with dates the customer asked for first, then due date, then the biggest quotes. Call, text, email, log it, next lead. Nothing reaches a customer until the rep sends it.

bullets.title: Email From Your Own Gmail
bullets.text: Connect Gmail once. Emails go from the rep's own address with their signature and photos attached.

bullets.title: Texts From Your Own Phone
bullets.text: Send the Text opens Messages with the draft filled in. On iPhone, the Kickback Send Text shortcut hands it to Messages with the photos attached.

bullets.title: Swipe or Use the Keyboard
bullets.text: In the iPhone app, swipe right to send and left to skip. On a desktop, J and K move through the queue and Enter confirms.

bullets.title: Every Touch Logged in Your CRM
bullets.text: With activity notes on, each logged touch is added to the estimate as a note with the rep, the time, the outcome and what was sent.

items.title: Pipeline and Digests
items.body: The Pipeline lists every enrolled estimate with its rep, amount, status and whether the sales call was recorded. Filter by status, rep or recording. Reps see their own estimates and owners see them all.

bullets.title: Drafts to Review
bullets.text: A morning push tells each rep how many drafts are waiting. You pick the hour, 7am by default.

bullets.title: Open Follow-Ups Digest
bullets.text: Owners get an email and a push at the end of the day listing every follow-up still due, with the rep and how many days it's overdue. It sends at 5pm unless you change it.

bullets.title: A Dashboard for the Numbers
bullets.text: Due today, open follow-ups, open value and wins in the last 30 days, above a list of overdue follow-ups.

sections.title: Automatic vs. You Confirm
sections.lede: Kickback keeps the list and writes the drafts. Nothing goes to a customer until a rep sends it.

sections.title: Works With Your Other Apps
sections.lede: Every Kickback app reads from the same CRM connection, so adding one means no new setup.

items.body: Follow-Up works the estimate until it's won. Costing picks up the job from there and matches supplier invoices to it, so you know what it cost.
Once a quote turns into a job, Warehouse tracks its material from the supplier's truck to the shelf to staging for the install.

items.q: Does Kickback ever text or email a customer on its own?
items.a: No. Every text and email waits in the Outbox until a rep sends it. Kickback doesn't place calls either. Reps call from their own phone.

items.q: Who do customers see the messages from?
items.a: The rep. Emails go through the rep's own Gmail with their signature. Texts open in Messages on the rep's phone or Mac, so they come from the rep's own number.

items.q: How does it write in my voice?
items.a: Drafts are written in first person from the rep who owns the estimate, kept short and plain, and tied to a detail from the quote. We can add notes on your company's tone when we set up your account, and reps can edit any draft before sending.
No. Without Siro, drafts are written from the estimate in your CRM. With Siro connected, the summary of the sales call goes into each draft too.
Yes. Owners, and anyone given the Cadence Editor role, can change the days and channels for Active, Thinking and Nurture, up to 10 touches each.

items.q: What gets written back to my CRM?
items.a: With activity notes turned on, each logged touch adds one note to the estimate with the rep, the time, the outcome and what was sent. A status change adds a note with the rep's reason.
